overview: PCOS is a common hormonal and metabolic condition that can affect periods, ovulation, fertility, and long-term metabolic health. It can occur at any body size and does not necessarily involve insulin resistance or higher weight.

lifestyle_tips: Maintain regular physical activity and reduce prolonged sitting.
Keep a consistent sleep routine.
Use sustainable habits rather than restrictive approaches.
Support stress management and emotional wellbeing.
Track menstrual patterns when useful.
diet_recommendations: Choose a balanced eating pattern built around vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes, and protein-rich foods.
Include fibre-rich carbohydrate sources and minimally processed foods.
Choose unsaturated fats such as nuts, seeds, and vegetable oils.
Drink water regularly and limit sugar-sweetened beverages.
Tailor food choices to personal preferences, culture, nutritional needs, and goals.

foods_to_avoid: Refined grains as the main carbohydrate source

exercise_recommendations: Aim for at least 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly, or an equivalent combination of moderate and vigorous activity.

Reduce prolonged sitting and add light movement throughout the day.
Choose activities that are enjoyable and sustainable.
monitoring_recommendations: Track menstrual cycle patterns and discuss persistent irregularity with a healthcare professional.
